examples.ko: 이 기사는 정치권의 부패상을 자세히 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This article shows the corruption in politics in detail.
The reporter investigated and reported on the corruption in public institutions.
People were very angry at the corruption in society.

examples.ko: 영화는 조선 말기의 부패상을 날카롭게 그려요.
examples.en: The film sharply portrays the corruption of the late Joseon period.
As soon as the corruption came to light, the mayor apologized.

examples.ko: 시민 단체가 그 회사의 부패상을 고발했어요.
examples.en: A citizens' group exposed the company's corrupt practices.

explain: '부패'는 썩거나 타락한 상태 자체를 말하고, '부패상'은 그 모습이 눈에 보이게 드러난 상황을 말해요. '드러나다, 폭로하다, 고발하다' 같은 말과 자주 쓰고 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '부패가 심하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: '부패' is corruption itself, while '부패상' is how that corruption actually shows up as a situation. It often goes with '드러나다', '폭로하다' and '고발하다', and appears mostly in news and writing. In everyday talk people say '부패가 심하다'.

examples.ko: 바다 위에 빨간 부표가 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A red buoy is floating on the sea.

examples.ko: 어부들은 부표를 보고 그물 위치를 찾아요.
examples.en: Fishermen find where their nets are by looking at the buoy.
We are careful so the boat doesn't hit the buoy.
The buoy drifted far away because of the waves.
The angler stopped the boat next to the buoy.

examples.ko: 항구 근처에는 안전을 알리는 부표가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many buoys marking safety near the harbor.

explain: 바다나 강에 띄워서 위치나 위험한 곳을 알리는 물건이에요. 낚싯줄에 달린 '찌'와 비슷해 보이지만, 부표는 그물이나 항로를 표시하는 큰 표지를 말해요. 뉴스에서는 양식장 '스티로폼 부표' 이야기가 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a float placed on the sea or a river to mark a position or a danger. It looks like a fishing '찌' (bobber), but a 부표 is a larger marker for nets or sea routes. In the news you often hear about styrofoam buoys at fish farms.

examples.ko: 남의 말에 부화뇌동하지 말고 직접 알아보세요.
examples.en: Don't just follow what others say; find out for yourself.

examples.ko: 친구들이 다 산다고 해서 부화뇌동해서 주식을 샀어요.
examples.en: Everyone said they were buying, so I blindly followed and bought stocks.
He is not someone who just goes along with the mood.
If you blindly follow rumors, you'll regret it later.

examples.ko: 회의에서 다들 부화뇌동하는 바람에 반대 의견이 없었어요.
examples.en: Since everyone just went along in the meeting, there were no opposing opinions.
You should be careful about following the crowd when you invest.

explain: 그냥 '따라 하다'와 달리, 줏대 없이 남에게 휩쓸린다는 비판이 들어 있어요. 보통 '~에 부화뇌동하다'로 쓰고, 칭찬하는 말로는 쓰지 않아요. 말할 때는 '휩쓸리다'나 '남 따라 하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '따라 하다' (to imitate), it carries criticism: following others without a mind of your own. It is usually used as '~에 부화뇌동하다' and never as praise. In casual speech, '휩쓸리다' or '남 따라 하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: This period was the heyday of Korean cinema's revival.
They say the 1990s were a golden revival period for Korean pop.
The city entered a period of revival, and people flocked to it.

examples.ko: 불교 문화의 부흥기에 많은 절이 지어졌어요.
examples.en: Many temples were built during the revival of Buddhist culture.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 요즘 새로운 부흥기를 누리고 있어요.
examples.en: That shop is enjoying a new boom these days.
Will a revival period come to our neighborhood again?

explain: '전성기'는 가장 잘나가던 때이고, '부흥기'는 약해졌다가 다시 힘차게 일어나는 시기에 더 잘 어울려요. 문화, 산업, 종교, 도시 이야기에 많이 쓰고 '맞이하다, 누리다'와 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: '전성기' is the peak time, while '부흥기' fits a time when something weak rises strongly again. It is common for culture, industry, religion and cities, and often goes with '맞이하다' and '누리다'.

examples.en: Dark clouds are gathering in the northern sky.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 북녘에 두고 온 고향을 그리워하세요.
examples.en: My grandfather misses the hometown he left in the north.

examples.ko: 북녘 땅을 밟아 보는 게 어머니의 소원이에요.
examples.en: My mother's wish is to set foot on northern soil.
Migratory birds are flying north.

examples.ko: 북녘 가족을 만나길 기다리는 분들이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people are waiting to meet their family in the north.
A cold wind is blowing in from the north today.

explain: 일상에서는 '북쪽'이라고 하고, '북녘'은 시나 노래, 글에서 자주 나와요. '북녘 땅', '북녘 동포'처럼 쓰면 보통 북한 지역을 가리켜요. '남녘', '동녘', '서녘'도 같은 짝이에요.
explain_en: In daily life people say '북쪽', while '북녘' shows up in poems, songs and writing. In phrases like '북녘 땅' and '북녘 동포' it usually refers to North Korea. '남녘', '동녘' and '서녘' are its counterparts.

en: with a scratching or ripping sound

examples.en: My back itched, so I scratched it hard with my nails.
The child tore the drawing paper with a ripping sound.
Dad swept the yard hard with a broom.

examples.ko: 지우개로 북북 문질러도 잘 안 지워져요.
examples.en: Even when I rub it hard with an eraser, it doesn't come off well.
I scratched my head hard while thinking.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 편지를 북북 찢어 버렸어요.
examples.en: I was angry, so I ripped the letter to pieces.

explain: 거칠게 긁거나 찢거나 문지를 때 나는 소리와 모습이에요. '박박'은 닦거나 긁을 때 쓰고, 종이나 천을 찢을 때는 '북북'이 더 자연스러워요. '긁다, 찢다, 문지르다' 같은 동사 앞에 와요.
explain_en: It describes the sound and look of scratching, tearing or rubbing roughly. '박박' is used for scrubbing or scratching, but for ripping paper or cloth, '북북' is more natural. It comes before verbs like '긁다', '찢다' and '문지르다'.

examples.en: I hit the drum hard with the drumstick.
I lost my drumstick, so I couldn't practice.

examples.ko: 공연 전에 북채를 두 개 준비했어요.
examples.en: I prepared two drumsticks before the performance.

examples.ko: 아이에게 북채를 쥐는 법을 가르쳐 줬어요.
examples.en: I taught the child how to hold a drumstick.
The drumstick broke, so I bought a new one.

examples.ko: 선생님이 북채를 높이 들고 박자를 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The teacher raised the drumstick high and showed us the beat.

explain: 풍물놀이나 판소리의 북처럼 한국 전통 북을 치는 막대를 말할 때 자연스러워요. 서양 드럼에는 보통 '드럼 스틱'이라고 해요. '북을 치다'와 함께 '북채를 잡다'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It sounds natural for the stick used on traditional Korean drums, such as in pungmul or pansori. For a Western drum set, people usually say '드럼 스틱'. Along with '북을 치다' (to beat a drum), you often hear '북채를 잡다' (to pick up the sticks).

examples.ko: 북풍한설이 몰아치는 날에는 밖에 나가기 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't want to go outside on days when the freezing north wind and snow rage.
Even in the bitter wind and snow, the children had a snowball fight.

examples.ko: 할머니는 북풍한설 속에 먼 길을 걸어오셨대요.
examples.en: They say my grandmother walked a long way in the bitter wind and snow.

examples.ko: 북풍한설을 견디고 핀 매화가 더 아름다워요.
examples.en: Plum blossoms that bloom after enduring the harsh winter are even more beautiful.

examples.ko: 그 시절에는 북풍한설에도 걸어서 학교에 다녔대요.
examples.en: They say that back then they walked to school even in the bitter winter storms.
Winter nights with the bitter wind and snow are really long.

explain: 매섭게 추운 겨울 날씨를 글이나 옛이야기처럼 말하는 표현이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '찬바람, 한파'라고 해요. 힘든 시련을 비유할 때도 '북풍한설을 견디다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It describes bitterly cold winter weather in a literary, storytelling way. In everyday talk people say '찬바람' or '한파'. It is also used figuratively for hardship, as in '북풍한설을 견디다'.

examples.ko: 분가를 하려면 먼저 집부터 구해야 해요.
examples.en: If you want to move out, you first need to find a place.
My older brother is preparing to move out this year.
Even after moving out, I visit my parents often.
What was your reason for deciding to move out?

examples.ko: 분가는 보통 결혼할 때 많이 해요.
examples.en: People usually move out of the family home when they get married.
The newlyweds got a small home when they moved out on their own.

explain: 결혼 같은 일로 부모님이나 큰집에서 나와 따로 살림을 차리는 것을 말해요. 그냥 '이사'와 달리 가족에서 독립해 새 가정을 이룬다는 느낌이 있어요. 요즘 일상에서는 '독립'이라는 말을 더 많이 쓰고, 반대로 다시 합치는 건 '합가'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means leaving your parents' or the main family's home, usually after marriage, to set up your own household. Unlike plain '이사' (moving), it carries the feeling of becoming a separate family. In daily talk '독립' is more common now, and the opposite, living together again, is '합가'.

examples.en: I moved out of my parents' home when I got married.
My younger sibling also plans to move out soon.

examples.ko: 아들이 직장 때문에 분가해서 따로 살아요.
examples.en: My son moved out because of his job and lives separately.
My uncle moved out a long time ago.
When would be a good time to move out?

examples.ko: 우리 부부는 아이가 태어나기 전에 분가해요.
examples.en: My spouse and I are moving out before the baby is born.

explain: 주로 결혼한 자녀가 부모님 집에서 나와 따로 사는 경우에 써서, 혼자 사는 '자취하다'와는 느낌이 달라요. 높이면 '분가하셨어요'라고 하고, 반대말은 '합가하다'예요. 요즘 대화에서는 '독립하다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when a married child leaves the parents' home to live separately, which feels different from '자취하다' (living alone). The honorific form is '분가하셨어요', and the opposite is '합가하다'. In conversation today '독립하다' is also very common.

examples.ko: 회사 노사 분규가 점점 길어지고 있어요.
examples.en: The labor dispute at the company is getting longer.

examples.ko: 두 마을 사이에 땅 문제로 분규가 생겼어요.
examples.en: A dispute arose between the two villages over land.
The union met with management to end the dispute.

examples.ko: 분규 때문에 공장이 한 달 동안 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The factory stopped for a month because of the dispute.

examples.ko: 오랜 분규 끝에 드디어 합의가 이루어졌어요.
examples.en: After a long dispute, an agreement was finally reached.
News about the school dispute was on the news.

explain: 노사나 단체, 마을 사이에서 의견이 부딪혀 시끄럽게 얽힌 싸움을 말해요. 뉴스에서 '노사 분규'로 많이 나오고, 친구끼리의 말다툼에는 쓰지 않아요. 비슷한 말로 '분쟁'이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to a noisy, tangled conflict between labor and management, groups or villages. It appears often in the news as '노사 분규', and is not used for an argument between friends. A similar word is '분쟁'.

examples.ko: 세금을 여섯 달에 나눠 분납할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can pay the tax in installments over six months.
I asked whether tuition can be paid in installments.

examples.ko: 분납을 신청하면 한 번에 내는 부담이 줄어요.
examples.en: If you apply for installments, the burden of paying at once is lower.
I am paying the insurance premium in installments.

examples.ko: 이 가격은 분납하면 조금 더 비싸요.
examples.en: This price is a bit higher if you pay in installments.
The installment period is up to twelve months.

explain: 세금, 등록금, 보험료처럼 큰 돈을 나눠서 내는 것을 공식적으로 말할 때 써요. 물건을 살 때는 '할부'라고 하는 경우가 많아요. 반대로 한 번에 내는 건 '일시납'이나 '일시불'이에요.
explain_en: It is the formal word for paying a large sum, such as taxes, tuition or insurance, in parts. When buying goods, people more often say '할부'. Paying all at once is '일시납' or '일시불'.

examples.en: The share for this gathering is five thousand won.
The association members paid their share of the construction costs.
The contribution went up so much that it's a heavy burden.
The deadline for paying the contribution is next week.
The contribution is a little different for each member.
I couldn't pay my share, so I got a call.

explain: 여러 사람이나 나라가 어떤 일의 비용을 나눠 맡아서 내는 돈이에요. 정기적으로 내는 '회비'와 달리 특정 사업이나 일의 비용을 나눌 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '방위비 분담금', '재건축 분담금'으로 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is the money that several people or countries pay as their share of the cost of something. Unlike a regular '회비' (membership fee), it is for the cost of a specific project or task. In the news you often hear '방위비 분담금' and '재건축 분담금'.

examples.en: A divider is installed in the middle of the road.
The car crashed into the divider.

examples.ko: 분리대 때문에 반대편으로 바로 건너갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Because of the divider, you can't cross straight to the other side.

examples.ko: 자전거 도로와 차도 사이에 분리대를 세웠어요.
examples.en: They put up a barrier between the bike path and the road.
The barrier in front of the construction site has fallen over.
I can see the opposite lane over the divider.

explain: 차선이나 길을 나누려고 세운 구조물이에요. 도로 한가운데 있는 건 '중앙분리대'라고 하는 경우가 많아요. 뉴스에서 교통사고 이야기를 할 때도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a structure built to separate lanes or paths. The one in the very middle of a road is often called '중앙분리대'. It also comes up often in news about traffic accidents.

examples.en: Children still lack judgment.
You develop better judgment as you get older.

examples.ko: 광고를 볼 때는 분별력 있게 고르는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: When you look at ads, it's important to choose with good judgment.
I was so angry that I lost my sense of judgment.

examples.ko: 인터넷 정보는 분별력을 가지고 봐야 해요.
examples.en: You should look at online information with discernment.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 분별력이 뛰어나서 믿을 만해요.
examples.en: He has excellent judgment, so he can be trusted.

explain: 옳고 그름이나 진짜와 가짜를 가려내는 힘이에요. '판단력'과 비슷하지만 분별력은 무엇이 맞고 틀린지 구별하는 데 더 초점이 있어요. '분별력이 있다/없다/생기다/잃다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the ability to tell right from wrong, or real from fake. It is close to '판단력', but '분별력' focuses more on distinguishing what is right and wrong. It is used as '분별력이 있다/없다/생기다/잃다'.

examples.en: It's really thoughtless of you to say that.
Thoughtless behavior makes things hard for everyone.
You're not a child, so why are you so thoughtless?
Everyone was shocked by his indiscreet words.
I apologize for my thoughtless behavior.
You end up regretting careless spending later.

explain: 앞뒤를 가리지 못하고 경솔하다는 뜻이라 사람이나 행동을 비판할 때 써요. '철없다'는 어린 느낌이 강하고, '분별없다'는 어른에게도 쓸 수 있어요. 반대는 '분별 있다'이고, 주로 '분별없는 행동/말'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means being careless without thinking things through, so it is used to criticize a person or an action. '철없다' feels childish, while '분별없다' can be used for adults too. The opposite is '분별 있다', and it is mostly used as '분별없는 행동/말'.

examples.en: If you spend money carelessly, it's gone quickly.
I'm sorry for losing my temper without thinking.
You shouldn't believe rumors without discernment.
He recklessly talked about other people's secrets.
The kids are running around recklessly, which is dangerous.
Don't make promises without thinking.

explain: 앞뒤를 따져 보지 않고 행동한다는 느낌이에요. '함부로'와 비슷한데, '함부로'가 더 일상적이고 '분별없이'는 조금 딱딱해요. '쓰다, 믿다, 말하다, 행동하다' 같은 동사와 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: It gives the feeling of acting without weighing things up. It is similar to '함부로', but '함부로' is more everyday and '분별없이' is a bit stiffer. It pairs often with verbs like '쓰다', '믿다', '말하다' and '행동하다'.

examples.ko: 이번 시험이 제 인생의 분수령이 될 거예요.
examples.en: This exam will be a turning point in my life.
This game is the watershed of this season.

examples.ko: 그 사건이 두 나라 관계의 분수령이 되었어요.
examples.en: That event became a turning point in relations between the two countries.
They say this week is the critical point of the negotiations.

examples.ko: 이 산이 두 강의 분수령 역할을 해요.
examples.en: This mountain acts as the divide between the two rivers.

examples.ko: 이 선거는 정치 변화의 분수령으로 불려요.
examples.en: This election is called a watershed for political change.

explain: 원래는 빗물이 서로 다른 쪽으로 갈라져 흐르는 산마루를 뜻하는데, 뉴스에서는 일이 크게 갈리는 중요한 고비로 많이 써요. '전환점'은 방향이 바뀌는 때이고, '분수령'은 이후 결과가 갈리는 결정적인 때라는 느낌이에요. 보통 '분수령이 되다'로 써요.

phrases.example: 이번 협상이 앞으로의 경제 정책에 분수령이 될 거예요.
phrases.en: These negotiations will be a watershed for future economic policy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산 이야기가 아니라 결과가 크게 갈리는 중요한 고비를 가리켜요. 뉴스, 연설, 글에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about mountains but about a critical point where outcomes split. Common in news, speeches and writing.

explain_en: Originally it is a ridge where rainwater flows in different directions, but in the news it is mostly used for an important point after which things go different ways. '전환점' is a time when direction changes, while '분수령' feels like the decisive point that splits the outcome. It is usually used as '분수령이 되다'.
